contracts.name: Background symmetry
contracts.definition: Symmetric, mildly asymmetric, or markedly asymmetric background.
contracts.applicability: Non-neonatal EEG; report A.2–A.10 separately by hemisphere when asymmetric.
criteria: Mild: consistent voltage difference <50% on an appropriate referential recording or frequency difference 0.5–1 Hz.
Marked: voltage difference >=50% or frequency difference >1 Hz.
Consistent means >80% of relevant instances or record.
exclusions: Do not measure voltage symmetry from longitudinal bipolar amplitude when referential comparison is unavailable.
engineering_choices: Choose the amplitude statistic and epoch aggregation for percent difference.

contracts.name: Predominant background frequency

source.section: A.2 Predominant Background Frequency When Most Awake or After Stimulation

contracts.definition: Band or tied bands most prominent when maximally awake or after stimulation.
contracts.applicability: Non-neonatal EEG; some terms may be imperfect for infants.
criteria: Categories: beta >13 Hz, alpha, theta, delta.
Report all 2 or 3 bands when equally prominent.
exclusions: Do not substitute a less-alert state when a more-awake/stimulated state is available.
engineering_choices: S01 gives no alpha/theta/delta boundaries or tie tolerance; version and review these separately.

contracts.name: Posterior dominant rhythm
contracts.definition: Posterior dominant rhythm present with frequency, absent, or unclear.
contracts.applicability: Non-neonatal EEG with interpretable eye-opening/closure testing.
criteria: Present requires attenuation with eye opening.
Wait >1 s after eye closure before measuring frequency; report to nearest 0.5 Hz.
exclusions: A posterior rhythm without demonstrated eye-opening attenuation is not present by this definition.
engineering_choices: Define attenuation threshold and minimum observation duration; S01 does not.

contracts.name: Continuity and low-voltage percent
contracts.definition: Continuity category from percent of a record/epoch occupied by attenuation or suppression.
contracts.applicability: Non-neonatal EEG; these voltage cutoffs differ from neonatal terminology.
criteria: Attenuation: lower activity >=10 µV and <50% of higher-voltage background; suppression: lower activity <10 µV.
Continuous: low-voltage percent <1%.
Nearly continuous: 1–9%, with qualifying periods >=1 s; report typical duration.
Discontinuous: alternating higher activity with 10–49% attenuation/suppression.
Burst attenuation/suppression: alternating higher activity with 50–99% attenuation/suppression.
Suppression/attenuation: >99%; suppressed when all activity <10 µV, attenuated when all activity <20 µV but not suppressed.
For noncontinuous records report attenuation or suppression percent using record/epoch as denominator.
Stimulus-induced periods are SI-attenuation or SI-suppression.
exclusions: >99% is not discontinuous or burst attenuation/suppression.
measurement_requirements: Peak-to-trough voltage in standard 10–20 longitudinal bipolar
engineering_choices: Fix analysis epoch, boundaries, and handling of mixed attenuation plus suppression.

contracts.name: Burst attenuation/suppression modifiers
contracts.definition: Timing, localization, morphology, highly epileptiform, and identical-burst descriptors.
contracts.applicability: Only burst attenuation or burst suppression.
criteria: Burst averages >=0.5 s and has >=4 phases (>=3 baseline crossings); maximum duration 30 s.
Report location as generalized, lateralized, bilateral independent, unilateral independent, or multifocal; report typical burst/interburst durations and sharpest component.

Highly epileptiform: >=2 spikes/sharp waves in most (>50%) bursts at mean >=1 Hz within a burst, where frequency = 1 / typical interpeak latency; alternatively a rhythmic potentially ictal-appearing pattern occurs in most (>50%) bursts. Table 1 states >=1 Hz for this alternative, while A.4.d does not repeat that cutoff. Record frequency and location.
Identical: first >=0.5 s of each burst, or each stereotyped cluster of >=2 bursts, is visually similar in all channels in most (>90%) bursts.
exclusions: RPP, BIRD, and seizure classification is outside this contract.
engineering_choices: Resolve the Table 1/A.4.d frequency-cutoff discrepancy; operationalize visual similarity and potentially ictal appearance.

contracts.name: Background reactivity
contracts.definition: Cerebral response to stimulation: reactive, unreactive, SIRPIDs-only, unclear, or unknown.
criteria: Qualifying change may be in cerebral voltage or frequency, including attenuation.
SIRPIDs-only: sole response is a stimulus-induced rhythmic, periodic, or ictal-appearing discharge.
Unclear: inadequate test, excessive artifact, or equivocal cerebral change. Unknown: not tested or maximally alert throughout.
exclusions: Muscle activity and eye blinks do not establish reactivity.
measurement_requirements: Repeat standardized noxious stimulation after an initially unreactive test
engineering_choices: Define stimulation protocol and cerebral-change threshold; S01 does not fully specify them.

contracts.name: State changes and N2 transients
contracts.definition: Sustained alertness/stimulation-related backgrounds with separate N2-transient characterization.
contracts.applicability: Non-neonatal EEG; spontaneous or stimulated transitions.
criteria: Present requires >=2 background types, each sustained >=60 s.
Stimulation should transition less-alert to more-alert/stimulated; spontaneous transitions qualify; the more-alert state is primary.
State changes virtually always imply reactivity; reactivity need not imply a state change when it lasts <60 s.
Categories: present with normal N2 transients; present with abnormal N2 transients; present without N2 transients; absent.
Describe K-complexes and spindles separately: present-normal, present-abnormal with abnormality, or absent.
exclusions: Reactivity lasting <60 s does not alone establish a state change.
engineering_choices: Define persistence across brief artifact and structured N2 abnormalities.

contracts.name: Cyclic alternating pattern of encephalopathy

source.section: A.7 Cyclic Alternating Pattern of Encephalopathy (CAPE)

contracts.definition: Regular spontaneous alternation of two backgrounds: present, absent, or unknown/unclear.
contracts.applicability: Non-neonatal encephalopathic EEG; components may include separately classified RPPs.
criteria: Each pattern lasts >=10 s and the pair alternates spontaneously/regularly for >=6 complete cycles; a cycle includes each state once.
Describe each pattern and typical duration; note awake/stimulated versus less-awake state when known.
If each pattern lasts >60 s, state-change criteria are also met.
exclusions: Stimulus-driven alternation alone is not the stated definition.
measurement_requirements: Optional coupling to respiration, heart rate, blood pressure, movement, muscle artifact, or pupils
engineering_choices: Define tolerance for 'regular'; S01 does not.

contracts.name: Background voltage
contracts.definition: High, normal, low, or suppressed peak-to-trough background voltage.
criteria: High: most/all activity >=150 µV.
Low: most/all activity <20 µV but not suppressed.
Suppressed: all activity <10 µV.
For nearly continuous/discontinuous records, use the higher-voltage portion.
exclusions: Do not apply to neonatal EEG.
engineering_choices: Define 'most/all' and numeric normal bounds; S01 does not.

contracts.name: Anterior-posterior gradient
contracts.definition: Expected AP gradient present, absent, or reversed.
contracts.applicability: Non-neonatal EEG with anterior and posterior derivations.
criteria: Present: clear persistent segment >=1 continuous min with lower-voltage/faster anterior and higher-voltage/slower posterior activity.
Reversed: same duration and paired criteria in the opposite direction.
exclusions: Voltage-only or frequency-only gradient is insufficient.

contracts.name: Breach effect
contracts.definition: Breach effect present with location, absent, or unclear.
contracts.applicability: EEG over or near a skull defect.
criteria: Present: higher amplitude and increased sharpness, mainly faster frequencies, versus the rest of brain and especially the contralateral homologous region.
exclusions: Sharp activity without the skull-defect spatial relationship is insufficient.
engineering_choices: Define comparison thresholds and whether defect metadata is mandatory.

contracts.name: Sporadic epileptiform discharge morphology
contracts.definition: Nonrhythmic, nonperiodic spikes, sharp waves, and polyspikes.
contracts.applicability: Non-neonatal EEG; localization may be added.
criteria: Spike: pointed transient distinct from background, duration >=20 ms and <70 ms at EEG baseline.
Sharp wave: same definition, duration >=70 ms and <=200 ms (source states 70–200 ms).
Polyspike: >=2 consecutive spikes with no interdischarge interval, total duration <0.5 s.
Typical, not required: diphasic/triphasic, apiculate, asymmetric slope, followed by slow wave or other background disruption.
exclusions: >=0.5-s spike trains may enter BIRD or highly epileptiform burst classification, outside scope.
engineering_choices: S01 does not quantify pointedness/background disruption or explicitly discuss the 200-ms endpoint; adjudicate boundary cases.

contracts.name: Sporadic epileptiform discharge prevalence
contracts.definition: Combined prevalence of spikes, polyspikes, and sharp waves.
contracts.applicability: Nonrhythmic, nonperiodic sporadic discharges in non-neonatal EEG.
criteria: Abundant: >=1/10 s, but not periodic.
Frequent: >=1/min and <1/10 s.
Occasional: >=1/h and <1/min.
Rare: <1/h.
When abundant, mean and maximum count per 10-s epoch may be recorded.
exclusions: Periodic discharges cannot be abundant sporadic discharges.
engineering_choices: S01 provides no explicit absent category; represent zero events separately pending review.

coverage.notes: All ages excluding neonates; critical care primary. Some infant terms imperfect. Voltage is peak-to-trough in standard 10–20 longitudinal bipolar; symmetry prefers referential. Consistent means >80%.
Categories, denominator, burst qualification and modifiers mapped.

coverage.section: C–H RPPs, seizures, BIRDs, IIC, reporting, other terms
